reasons.reason: The foci sit on the major axis, and how far apart they are comes from the gap between the two semi-axes, five minus three, so the focal distance works out to two.
For an ellipse, c squared equals a squared minus b squared, which is twenty-five minus nine, so c is four. The foci are at plus and minus four, eight apart.
Split the octagon into eight triangles from the centre, each with two sides of length one and a forty-five degree angle between them. Each has area root two over four, so eight give two root two.
An inscribed square has area two and the whole circle has area pi, and an octagon with only eight sides should land roughly midway between them, which puts its area at about two and a half.
Compare with the perfect square x squared minus six x plus nine: the constant nine has root three, and for the expression to stay positive k has to sit beyond plus or minus three.
A parabola opening upward stays above zero for every x exactly when it has no real roots, so the discriminant k squared minus thirty-six must be negative, giving k strictly between minus six and six.
Rationalising by multiplying top and bottom by root three plus one gives four plus two root three over two, and that reduces neatly to two plus root three for the squared value.
Rationalising gives x equal to four plus two root three over two, so x is two plus root three. Squaring that gives four plus four root three plus three, which is seven plus four root three.
Side BC is opposite the thirty degree angle and AC is opposite the forty-five, so the law of sines gives BC equal to ten times one half divided by root two over two, five root two.
Dropping a perpendicular from C, the side of length ten projects through the cosine of thirty degrees, and ten times root three over two gives five root three for side BC.
